headline: All eleven art modules have landed: 1,877 sprites and 1,272 tiles, every pixel generated from code. A blind A/B critic scored the town against the Stardew density reference and lost 10-0; its findings have gone back to the level designer. Five maps now load clean at 60fps. The three quests, the dungeon, the boss, audio and dialogue are all in build.

findings.text: Blind A/B vs the Stardew reference: the town reads as a floor plan (ground drawn first, objects sprinkled on) rather than a scene. Fix: halve the open plaza and fill the reclaimed space with tall overlapping structure — trees first, then fences, hedges, stalls — placed to CROSS path edges and building bases.

Measured: most-repeated pixel-identical tile covers 11.9% of the frame (reference: 2.5%). Tonal contrast 0.148 vs the reference's 0.268 — there are no true darks in the frame. Zero trees on screen; the reference has eight.
Buildings sit on axis-aligned rectangular dirt pads with hard straight edges; the critic read them as a tilemap bug rather than as yards.
No prop casts a ground shadow — the 1px dark rim is an outline, not a shadow, so every prop reads as a sticker on the floor.
The fountain is too small and too low-contrast to anchor the square it sits in; eight identical flower planters repeat across open lawn.
The dynamic light layer is the game's genuine advantage over the reference and is under-exploited — only two small pools in the whole frame.

A session token limit terminated nine in-flight agents mid-edit. Four partial edits were repaired (Web Audio typed-array generics, a half-written event helper, an unexported map symbol); all agents resumed from their transcripts rather than restarting.
Phaser getFrame() returns the __BASE frame for unknown names, so every missing-art guard was drawing the entire 2048px atlas across the scene.
Tile families were keyed by leaf name, so tile/woods/grass_* merged with tile/town/grass_* and the town field rendered as a two-tone checkerboard.
edgePixels treated a tile's own border as a material edge, putting a lit line on the top row of every interior tile — a horizontal band across every path and every water surface in the game.
Grass variants were tone-mismatched and non-periodic, producing per-tile seams and brightness checkerboarding. Now seamless and rank-quantised.
Flagstone stamped one identical stone pattern on every tile; now a per-tile cellular partition with the mortar groove and lit bevel on separate pixels.
One agent's in-progress edit broke every other agent's art build. Modules now load dynamically and a broken one is skipped and reported.

comparisons.title: Town Square vs Stardew Valley world density
comparisons.verdict: Blind A/B: the reference wins all ten criteria. Building facades and the dynamic light layer are ours to keep; the ground layer, prop shadows and the absence of trees are what lose it.

comparisons.title: Festival Plaza vs Stardew Night Market
comparisons.verdict: The event transformation reads: string lights, bunting, a lit ceremonial carpet, stalls and a gathered crowd. Trial lanterns still need mounts.
